pageCache.pageTitle: Oak Farm Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
At Oak Farm Primary School, we actively promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. These values help children understand their rights and responsibilities, respect others, make positive choices and develop the knowledge and attitudes they need to participate positively in life in modern Britain.
British Values are woven throughout school life rather than taught as a one-off topic. They are explicitly explored through our PSHE curriculum and whole-school assemblies, as well as through subjects such as Religious Education and History. Children also experience these values in practice through pupil voice, school rules and responsibilities, collaborative learning and opportunities to discuss different viewpoints. Our aim is for every child to learn to respect, understand, belong and thrive within our diverse school community and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Oak Farm Primary School - Zone of Regulation
pageCache.text:
Zone of Regulation
At Oak Farm Primary School, we place pupils’ mental health and emotional wellbeing alongside their academic development. We want every child to feel safe, valued, listened to and that they belong within our school community.
The Zones of Regulation approach is used in every classroom at Oak Farm to help children understand and talk about their emotions. Pupils learn that feelings can be grouped into different ‘zones’ and develop strategies to help them recognise how they are feeling and what they may need to regulate themselves.
Zones of Regulation displays and resources are available in each classroom, giving children a consistent language for discussing emotions across the school. Adults use this approach to support pupils to identify their emotions, understand how these can affect their behaviour and learning, and choose appropriate strategies to help them feel ready to learn.
Importantly, we teach children that all emotions are valid. The aim is not to always be in one particular zone, but to develop the self-awareness and strategies needed to manage different emotions successfully.
Zones of regulation is one part of our wider PSHE curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Oak Farm Primary School - Golden Rules
pageCache.text:
Golden Rules
At Oak Farm Primary School, our approach to behaviour is built around three simple, consistent principles:
Be Ready • Be Safe • Be Respectful
These expectations provide a common language for behaviour across the school. They help children understand what positive behaviour looks like, while ensuring that adults respond calmly, consistently and predictably.
The principles apply everywhere and to everyone, but what they look like in practice will vary depending on a child’s age and the context — from the classroom and playground to the lunch hall, corridors and assemblies.
Click on the sections below to see how Be Ready, Be Safe and Be Respectful are taught and demonstrated across different phases and areas of Oak Farm.

pageCache.pageTitle: Oak Farm Primary School - PE/Sport premium
pageCache.text:
PE/Sport premium
At Oak Farm Primary School, we want every child to develop the confidence, skills and positive attitudes they need to enjoy physical activity and lead healthy, active lives. We recognise the important role that high-quality physical education, sport and active play have in supporting pupils’ physical health, wellbeing, teamwork, resilience and wider personal development.
The PE and Sport Premium funding is used strategically to strengthen the quality of our PE provision, increase opportunities for pupils to be physically active and ensure that improvements are sustainable.
Our priorities include:
Developing the knowledge, confidence and expertise of teachers and support staff so that pupils receive consistently high-quality PE lessons.
Providing a well-sequenced and ambitious PE curriculum that develops pupils’ knowledge, skills and physical confidence from EYFS through to Year 6.
Reviewing and updating PE resources and equipment to support effective curriculum delivery.
Using monitoring, pupil voice and participation information to identify strengths and areas for further development within PE and school sport.
Providing appropriate professional development, coaching and support for staff.
Increasing opportunities for pupils to participate in a broad range of sports, physical activities and competitive events.
Developing lunchtime provision so that pupils have access to purposeful, structured and enjoyable physical activities.
Supporting midday supervisors and other staff to lead active games and activities during lunchtimes.
Providing a varied programme of extra-curricular clubs and activities that encourages pupils of different ages, interests and abilities to participate.
Identifying and supporting pupils who are less physically active or who may experience barriers to participating in sport and physical activity.
Developing pupil leadership through opportunities such as Sports Leaders and other pupil-led activities.
Working with external partners and local organisations to broaden the sporting opportunities available to our pupils.
Ensuring that PE and Sport Premium funding contributes to sustainable improvements that continue to benefit pupils beyond the period of funding.
Measuring the impact
We will evaluate the impact of our PE and Sport Premium funding through:
Monitoring the quality and consistency of PE teaching and curriculum implementation.
Gathering pupil voice to understand pupils’ experiences, enjoyment and confidence in PE and sport.
Reviewing participation in lunchtime activities, after-school clubs, competitions and sporting events.
Monitoring the participation of different groups of pupils to ensure that opportunities are inclusive and accessible.
Evaluating the impact of staff professional development on teachers’ confidence, subject knowledge and practice.
Reviewing the range and quality of PE and sports equipment and resources.
Evaluating progress against our PE action plan and identifying priorities for further improvement.
Our aim is for all pupils at Oak Farm Primary School to be physically active, confident and motivated, developing positive habits and an enjoyment of physical activity that can continue throughout their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Oak Farm Primary School - Reading and Phonics
pageCache.text:
Reading and Phonics
At Oak Farm Primary School, we believe that a high-quality, rich and diverse English curriculum should inspire a lifelong love of reading, writing and learning. We want every child to become a confident reader who can engage with, enjoy and understand a wide range of texts.
Alongside daily English lessons, every child has a dedicated reading lesson each day from 9:00–9:30am, ensuring that reading is at the heart of our curriculum. In EYFS and Key Stage 1, we teach early reading through Read Write Inc. Phonics, a systematic synthetic phonics programme. Since our Ofsted inspection, we have worked closely with our English Hub and Read Write Inc. specialists to further strengthen the teaching of phonics and early reading across the school.
In Key Stage 2, children follow our bespoke reading curriculum, carefully structured around high-quality key texts. Pupils experience a diverse range of fiction, non-fiction and poetry and are explicitly taught the knowledge and skills they need to read fluently, understand meaning, make connections and think deeply about what they read.
We also look for opportunities to bring reading and literature to life. Each year, the whole school celebrates World Book Day, and our pupils take part in the Vanguard Learning Trust Poetry Competition, alongside other reading and writing opportunities throughout the year. We are fortunate to have dedicated Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 libraries, which children visit weekly, giving them regular opportunities to explore new authors, discover different genres and, most importantly, develop a genuine love of reading.
